messages:
maria: Heads-up — my TF plan for the per-model flags change shows the configmap resource will be recreated when the model list updates, which will trigger rolling restarts for ~50 replicas. Is that intended?

aj: Oof, recreating CM = pod restarts. Did the plan show the CM name or a checksum annotation getting bumped?

maria: It’s the CM name (we’re currently using model-specific names: model-config-${model}.yaml). The new change consolidates some keys and then updates name generation. plan snippet:```~ aws_s3_object.model_flags -> /configmaps/data/model-config-bert.yaml will be replaced```

kevin: Why are we changing names instead of content? That makes deployments noisy. We should keep stable CM names and use a hash annotation for content changes.

ida: Agreed. The hot-path for runtime knobs requires stable mounts so pods can update in-place when annotation checksum changes. Otherwise K8s treats as new configmap.

maria: I tried adding the checksum annotation in the module, but TF provider does not compute the hash for nested for_each properly in our current module layout.

aj: Can we add a post-processing step (local-exec) that computes sha256 of the rendered yaml and adds annotation? Not ideal but quick.

kevin: local-exec is brittle in CI. Better to refactor module to render a single map of model->yaml and compute hash with templatefile + sha256; then we can keep CM name stable: e.g. "model-config-${model}" and annotation "config-checksum: ${sha256(content)}".

maria: I sketched a patch in the branch. Also discovered the secret-sync lambda only watches secrets by name, not by annotation, so even if we switch to checksum annotation, secret rotations may not trigger the sync. config-bot posted: [secret-sync-lambda] detected change? (automated)

config-bot: secret-sync-lambda: last run 2026-02-18T14:02:01Z — scanning secrets by tag: env=prod. No change detected for model creds.

ida: That lambda is older tech. We have two options: update the lambda to watch annotation/labels on configmaps (needs IAM + eventbridge change), or add an explicit secret rotation webhook that posts to the lambda. Which is less invasive?

aj: Webhook is easier short term. Eventbridge + iam is more robust but requires infra changes and tests. For this rollout I'd vote webhook + follow-up ticket to migrate to eventbridge.

maria: Acceptable. I’ll change TF to stable names + checksum annotation, add a small webhook in front of secret-sync that accepts a model id and triggers sync. Quick question: will a checksum-only change cause a rolling restart?

kevin: If we add annotation to the configmap (metadata.annotations) and update it, K8s will update the configmap object but that alone won't restart pods. Pods get new contents mounted automatically for projected volumes, but many apps only read config at startup. Our runtime supports live reload on SIGHUP when file content updates (we wrote that bit for runtime knobs) — but only if the app watches the file. Most model servers do. Confirm per-model container?

maria: The model server image has a watcher that reloads on file change for /etc/model-config/flags.yaml. So no restart required. Good.

ida: Remember to add a compatibility flag: if older servers are still running (no watcher), we need a canary rollout plan for the CM change (canary label on deployment).

maria: Will do. Plan: 1) refactor TF module to use stable names + sha256 annotation; 2) add secret rotation webhook to trigger secret-sync lambda; 3) create canary rollout (10% of replicas) for first deploy; 4) update infra runbook. I’ll open PR with these changes.

aj: Ping me in the PR for a quick review — I’ll check the TF sha256 implementation and CI implications. Also add a note in the terraform state migration doc to rename the existing CM resources to avoid duplicate resources in the state.

kevin: Also add a pre-apply check that fails if more than X pods would be restarted (safety guard). We have a small script dot-ops/gate/check-cm-recreate.sh that can diff the plan and refuse if recreates > 5 for prod clusters. Reuse it.

maria: Good call — I’ll wire that into the pre-apply CI job.

ida: Tagging owners: @kevin for runtime behavior, @aj for TF module, @maria for PR. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — opening PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/compare/branch/feature/permodel-flag-stable-names (will post when ready).
